Bot: WhatsApp Away Auto-Reply Bot with Friendly Emojis

Summary:
A production-ready WhatsApp bot that acts as the account owner’s smart away assistant. When the owner is offline, busy, outside business hours, or manually marked as unavailable, the bot replies automatically with a friendly emoji-rich message, sets expectations, and optionally captures the sender’s request for later follow-up.

The bot is the brain service only. It runs as a single Node.js ESM process and connects to WhatsApp through CookMyBots managed transport. CookMyBots handles the WhatsApp connection and delivery layer, while this service handles rules, state, message decisions, templates, cooldowns, and optional persistence.

Product goals:
The main product goal is to prevent missed WhatsApp conversations from feeling ignored. If someone messages while the owner is unavailable, the bot should respond quickly, warmly, and clearly with emojis such as 😊, 👋, ⏰, or 🙏.

1) Provide automatic away replies when the owner is not online or has enabled away mode.
2) Let the owner configure message text, emojis, business hours, cooldowns, and exceptions.
3) Avoid annoying users by replying only once per contact within a configurable time window.
4) Support simple commands over WhatsApp so the owner can turn away mode on or off without opening an admin dashboard.
5) Keep the behavior safe for production by logging decisions, handling duplicate messages, and preventing response loops.
6) Support both simple personal use and small-business use cases, such as replying with opening hours, estimated response time, and urgent contact instructions.

A good default away response could be: Hi 👋 Thanks for your message! I’m currently offline, but I’ll get back to you as soon as possible 😊 If it’s urgent, please send the word URGENT.

High-level architecture:
The service should be designed as a single Node.js ESM application that receives normalized message events from CookMyBots managed transport and sends response instructions back through the same managed transport integration. It should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not depend on WhatsApp Cloud API environment variables.

The architecture can be split into practical modules inside the same process:

1) Transport adapter: Receives inbound message events from CookMyBots and sends outbound messages through CookMyBots. This module should hide transport details from the rest of the bot.

2) Message router: Classifies messages as owner commands, normal customer messages, group messages, media messages, repeated messages, or unsupported events.

3) Availability engine: Decides whether the owner is available. It should combine manual away mode, business-hours rules, temporary snooze periods, and optional inactivity-based status.

4) Auto-reply decision engine: Decides whether to reply. It checks availability, contact allowlists or blocklists, group settings, cooldown windows, previous replies, and anti-loop protection.

5) Template engine: Selects and renders a friendly response using the configured text, emojis, sender name if available, current time context, and optional urgency instructions.

6) Command handler: Allows the owner to control the bot from WhatsApp using commands such as away on, away off, status, set message, and set hours.

7) Persistence layer: Uses MongoDB for production persistence if available. For a minimal setup, simple in-memory maps can be used, but they reset on service restart and are best for testing or lightweight personal use.

8) Observability and audit logs: Records key decisions such as inbound message received, reply skipped due to cooldown, reply sent, owner command applied, and configuration changed.

The bot should treat the owner’s own WhatsApp number as an admin identity. Admin messages are commands and should never trigger an away auto-reply. Customer messages are evaluated against the away rules.

Data model:
The data model should be small and focused. MongoDB is recommended for production so configuration, cooldowns, and reply history survive restarts. In-memory maps can be used for a simpler prototype.

1) BotConfig
Fields should include ownerId, botEnabled, awayModeEnabled, awayMessage, emojiStyle, businessHours, timezone, replyCooldownMinutes, respondInGroups, respondToUnknownOnly, urgentKeyword, updatedAt, and createdAt.

2) ContactState
Fields should include contactId, displayName, lastInboundAt, lastAutoReplyAt, lastMessagePreview, isBlocked, isVip, tags, conversationStatus, and updatedAt. This allows per-contact cooldowns and exceptions.

3) AwaySession
Fields should include ownerId, active, reason, startedAt, endsAt, createdByCommand, and temporaryMessageOverride. This supports temporary away states like away for 2 hours.

4) MessageLog
Fields should include messageId, direction, contactId, messageType, textPreview, receivedAt, decision, replySent, skipReason, and relatedCommand. This is useful for debugging and duplicate handling.

5) CommandAudit
Fields should include commandName, issuedBy, rawText, success, errorMessage, configChanges, and createdAt. This gives accountability for configuration changes.

6) TemplateConfig
Fields should include templateName, language, bodyText, emojiSet, enabled, useBusinessHoursVariant, useUrgentVariant, and updatedAt.

Recommended indexes include unique messageId for idempotency, contactId plus lastAutoReplyAt for cooldown checks, and ownerId for configuration lookup. Message logs can be retained for a limited period to reduce storage usage.

Key flows:
Inbound customer message flow:

1) CookMyBots delivers a normalized inbound WhatsApp message event to the bot brain service.
2) The transport adapter validates the event shape and passes it to the message router.
3) The router ignores unsupported system events and detects whether the sender is the owner/admin.
4) If the message is from the owner, it is passed to the command handler instead of the auto-reply engine.
5) If the message is from a customer, the availability engine checks manual away mode, temporary away sessions, and business-hours rules.
6) If the owner is available, the bot records the message and sends no auto-reply.
7) If the owner is unavailable, the decision engine checks whether the contact is blocked, whether the chat is a group, whether a cooldown is active, and whether this message was already processed.
8) If allowed, the template engine creates a friendly emoji response.
9) The bot sends the response through CookMyBots managed transport.
10) The bot stores the reply timestamp and message decision for future cooldown and audit purposes.

Owner turns away mode on:

1) Owner sends a command such as away on Out for lunch 😊.
2) The command handler verifies that the sender is an authorized admin.
3) The bot updates BotConfig or creates an active AwaySession.
4) The bot confirms to the owner with a short message such as Away mode is now on 😊.
5) Future customer messages receive the configured away response subject to cooldown rules.

Owner turns away mode off:

1) Owner sends away off.
2) The bot disables the active away state.
3) The bot confirms that auto-replies are paused.
4) Future customer messages are logged but not auto-replied unless business-hours rules still mark the owner unavailable.

Cooldown behavior:

1) A customer messages while away mode is active.
2) The bot replies once.
3) If the same customer sends more messages within the cooldown window, the bot does not keep replying.
4) After the cooldown expires, a new message can receive a fresh away reply.

Urgent keyword flow:

1) The away message can tell customers to send URGENT for priority attention.
2) If a customer sends the urgent keyword, the bot can respond with a special acknowledgement and mark the contact as urgent in ContactState.
3) The bot should not promise emergency handling unless the owner explicitly configures that wording.

Tech stack:
The service should be a single Node.js application using ESM modules. It should run as one process and contain the bot logic, command handling, availability rules, template rendering, persistence access, and CookMyBots transport integration.

WhatsApp connectivity should be handled only through CookMyBots managed transport. The bot project should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not require WHATSAPPTOKEN, WHATSAPPPHONENUMBERID, or WHATSAPPVERIFYTOKEN. The service should only need the credentials or connection settings required by CookMyBots for the managed transport.

Persistence should use MongoDB when production durability is needed. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable for local testing, demos, or a personal bot where restart persistence is not required. No additional databases, cache servers, brokers, or external queue systems should be introduced.

For any optional media or export storage, use object storage or simple filesystem storage described generically. This bot does not require image or file storage for the core away-reply use case.

Deployment should be a generic Node.js server in the cloud or any always-on environment capable of running a single Node.js service. Configuration should be provided through environment variables or a secure runtime configuration mechanism. The process should support graceful startup, graceful shutdown, and health checks.

Non-functional requirements:
Reliability:

1) Use messageId-based idempotency so the same inbound message does not trigger duplicate replies.
2) Store lastAutoReplyAt per contact to enforce cooldowns.
3) Fail safely by logging errors and avoiding repeated send attempts that could spam users.
4) Keep default behavior conservative: reply only in direct chats unless group replies are explicitly enabled.

Security:

1) Only authorized owner/admin numbers can run commands.
2) Customer messages should never be able to change bot configuration.
3) Logs should store previews rather than full sensitive conversations where possible.
4) Secrets for CookMyBots and MongoDB should be kept outside source control.

Privacy:

1) Retain only the data needed for reply decisions and support.
2) Allow message logs to expire after a configured retention period.
3) Provide a command or admin operation to clear a contact’s stored state if needed.

User experience:

1) Replies should feel human, concise, and friendly.
2) Emojis should be configurable because some businesses prefer a professional tone while personal users may want a casual tone.
3) The bot should not over-reply during a conversation.
4) The away message should set realistic expectations, such as expected response time or business hours.

Operations:

1) Expose a simple health status for process monitoring.
2) Log structured events for inbound messages, decisions, sends, skips, and command changes.
3) Include safe defaults for cooldown, business hours, and group behavior.
4) Support configuration backup through MongoDB records or simple exported configuration.

Bot commands:
• away on — Enables manual away mode immediately. Customer messages will receive the configured emoji-rich auto-reply, subject to cooldown and contact rules. (usage: away on) [availability]
• away off — Disables manual away mode. The bot stops sending manual away replies, though business-hours rules may still apply if enabled. (usage: away off) [availability]
• away for — Turns on away mode for a temporary duration, then automatically returns to the previous availability state. (usage: away for 2h In a meeting 😊) [availability]
• status — Shows whether the bot is enabled, whether away mode is active, the current away message, cooldown settings, and business-hours status. (usage: status) [admin]
• set message — Updates the default auto-reply text. The message can include emojis and should clearly explain when the owner will respond. (usage: set message Hi 👋 I’m offline right now, but I’ll reply as soon as I can 😊) [configuration]
• set cooldown — Sets how long the bot should wait before sending another away reply to the same contact. (usage: set cooldown 60m) [configuration]
• set hours — Configures business hours so the bot can automatically reply outside the owner’s normal availability window. (usage: set hours Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00) [configuration]
• groups on — Allows away replies in group chats. This should be disabled by default to avoid noisy group behavior. (usage: groups on) [configuration]
• groups off — Disables away replies in group chats. Direct customer chats can still receive replies. (usage: groups off) [configuration]
• preview — Shows the owner exactly what customers will receive if they message while the bot is in away mode. (usage: preview) [testing]

# WhatsApp Away Reply Bot

This is a CookMyBots managed WhatsApp brain service.

CookMyBots handles WhatsApp connection, phone pairing, sessions, and message routing. This project does not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks, Baileys sessions, QR login, or phone pairing.

The bot is an AI-first away auto-reply assistant. When CookMyBots routes a WhatsApp message to this service, the bot uses CookMyBots AI Gateway to generate a brief, friendly WhatsApp-native away reply with appropriate emojis.

## Owner knowledge

The raw owner prompt is preserved exactly as:

Create a bot that automatically responds to messages when not online,with emojis

This is the only source of truth for what the bot knows. The bot must not invent business details, products, prices, contacts, locations, delivery details, payment details, support policies, moderation rules, or community behavior.

If someone asks for details that the owner did not provide, the bot should politely say that the owner has not provided that detail yet.

## Public behavior

There are no slash commands, menus, or command maps.

Users simply send normal WhatsApp messages. The bot replies as an away responder when AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED is enabled.

Public behavior:

1) Responds naturally to WhatsApp DMs routed by CookMyBots.
2) Responds briefly in groups or communities when CookMyBots routes those messages.
3) Acknowledges the incoming message.
4) Explains that the owner is currently unavailable or not online.
5) Invites the sender to wait for a direct reply later.
6) Uses friendly emojis without overusing them.
7) Says clearly when the requested detail was not supplied by the owner.

## Endpoint

CookMyBots calls this endpoint:

POST /webhook/cookmybots/whatsapp

The request must include:

X-CookMyBots-Webhook-Secret: your configured CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET

The endpoint returns:

{ "ok": true, "reply": "..." }

## Environment variables

PORT
The HTTP port. Defaults to 3000.

CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET
Used to verify that inbound webhook calls came from CookMyBots. Configure this in the deployed service environment.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_ENDPOINT
CookMyBots AI Gateway base URL. It must be a base URL such as https://api.cookmybots.com/api/ai. The bot appends /chat itself.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY
CookMyBots AI Gateway key. The bot sends it using Authorization: Bearer, but never logs the key.

AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED
Optional. Defaults to true when missing. Set to false, 0, off, no, or disabled to pause auto replies.

OWNER_DISPLAY_NAME
Optional. Defaults to the owner when missing. Used only to help AI phrase natural away replies.

AI_TIMEOUT_MS
Optional. Defaults to 600000 milliseconds.

AI_MAX_RETRIES
Optional. Defaults to 2 retries.

CONCURRENCY
Optional. Defaults to 20 global simultaneous AI jobs. The bot also uses a per-chat lock so one chat cannot stack multiple AI replies at once.

## Local setup

1) Install dependencies:

npm install

2) Copy the sample environment file:

cp .env.sample .env

3) Fill in CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET and COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY.

4) Start development mode:

npm run dev

## Local test

You can test without WhatsApp transport by using /test:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/test \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hi, are you there?"}'

## Deployment

Deploy as one Node.js service on Render or a similar host.

Use:

Build command: npm run build
Start command: npm start

Do not create a worker process or queue process. This project runs as a single Node.js process.

## Logging

The bot logs startup, environment sanity booleans, managed webhook handling, AI gateway start, AI gateway success, AI gateway failure, and occasional memory usage.

Secrets are never logged.

## Database

No database is required for this version. The bot keeps only a small bounded in-memory conversation context per chat to help AI respond naturally during the current process lifetime.

# WhatsApp Community Assistant Bot

This is a CookMyBots managed WhatsApp AI representative.

## Important

This project is the bot brain only. CookMyBots owns the WhatsApp connection/session and forwards inbound WhatsApp messages to this deployed app.

This bot does not use a fixed Telegram-style command system.

Instead:

- the owner prompt is stored as raw knowledge
- AI reads that knowledge
- AI determines what the bot represents
- AI determines whether it is for a community, business, project, support desk, school, creator, group, event, or something else
- AI determines the user intent
- AI replies naturally in WhatsApp DMs and groups

## Transport endpoint

CookMyBots calls:

```txt
POST /webhook/cookmybots/whatsapp
```

The endpoint returns:

```json
{ "ok": true, "reply": "..." }
```

## Required AI config

```env
COOKMYBOTS_AI_ENDPOINT=
COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY=
```

## Local test

```bash
npm install
cp .env.sample .env
npm run dev
```

Then:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/test \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Who are you and what can you help with?"}'
```

state.planMarkdown:
Bot: WhatsApp Away Auto-Reply Bot with Friendly Emojis

Summary:
A production-ready WhatsApp bot that acts as the account owner’s smart away assistant. When the owner is offline, busy, outside business hours, or manually marked as unavailable, the bot replies automatically with a friendly emoji-rich message, sets expectations, and optionally captures the sender’s request for later follow-up.

The bot is the brain service only. It runs as a single Node.js ESM process and connects to WhatsApp through CookMyBots managed transport. CookMyBots handles the WhatsApp connection and delivery layer, while this service handles rules, state, message decisions, templates, cooldowns, and optional persistence.

Product goals:
The main product goal is to prevent missed WhatsApp conversations from feeling ignored. If someone messages while the owner is unavailable, the bot should respond quickly, warmly, and clearly with emojis such as 😊, 👋, ⏰, or 🙏.

1) Provide automatic away replies when the owner is not online or has enabled away mode.
2) Let the owner configure message text, emojis, business hours, cooldowns, and exceptions.
3) Avoid annoying users by replying only once per contact within a configurable time window.
4) Support simple commands over WhatsApp so the owner can turn away mode on or off without opening an admin dashboard.
5) Keep the behavior safe for production by logging decisions, handling duplicate messages, and preventing response loops.
6) Support both simple personal use and small-business use cases, such as replying with opening hours, estimated response time, and urgent contact instructions.

A good default away response could be: Hi 👋 Thanks for your message! I’m currently offline, but I’ll get back to you as soon as possible 😊 If it’s urgent, please send the word URGENT.

High-level architecture:
The service should be designed as a single Node.js ESM application that receives normalized message events from CookMyBots managed transport and sends response instructions back through the same managed transport integration. It should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not depend on WhatsApp Cloud API environment variables.

The architecture can be split into practical modules inside the same process:

1) Transport adapter: Receives inbound message events from CookMyBots and sends outbound messages through CookMyBots. This module should hide transport details from the rest of the bot.

2) Message router: Classifies messages as owner commands, normal customer messages, group messages, media messages, repeated messages, or unsupported events.

3) Availability engine: Decides whether the owner is available. It should combine manual away mode, business-hours rules, temporary snooze periods, and optional inactivity-based status.

4) Auto-reply decision engine: Decides whether to reply. It checks availability, contact allowlists or blocklists, group settings, cooldown windows, previous replies, and anti-loop protection.

5) Template engine: Selects and renders a friendly response using the configured text, emojis, sender name if available, current time context, and optional urgency instructions.

6) Command handler: Allows the owner to control the bot from WhatsApp using commands such as away on, away off, status, set message, and set hours.

7) Persistence layer: Uses MongoDB for production persistence if available. For a minimal setup, simple in-memory maps can be used, but they reset on service restart and are best for testing or lightweight personal use.

8) Observability and audit logs: Records key decisions such as inbound message received, reply skipped due to cooldown, reply sent, owner command applied, and configuration changed.

The bot should treat the owner’s own WhatsApp number as an admin identity. Admin messages are commands and should never trigger an away auto-reply. Customer messages are evaluated against the away rules.

Data model:
The data model should be small and focused. MongoDB is recommended for production so configuration, cooldowns, and reply history survive restarts. In-memory maps can be used for a simpler prototype.

1) BotConfig
Fields should include ownerId, botEnabled, awayModeEnabled, awayMessage, emojiStyle, businessHours, timezone, replyCooldownMinutes, respondInGroups, respondToUnknownOnly, urgentKeyword, updatedAt, and createdAt.

2) ContactState
Fields should include contactId, displayName, lastInboundAt, lastAutoReplyAt, lastMessagePreview, isBlocked, isVip, tags, conversationStatus, and updatedAt. This allows per-contact cooldowns and exceptions.

3) AwaySession
Fields should include ownerId, active, reason, startedAt, endsAt, createdByCommand, and temporaryMessageOverride. This supports temporary away states like away for 2 hours.

4) MessageLog
Fields should include messageId, direction, contactId, messageType, textPreview, receivedAt, decision, replySent, skipReason, and relatedCommand. This is useful for debugging and duplicate handling.

5) CommandAudit
Fields should include commandName, issuedBy, rawText, success, errorMessage, configChanges, and createdAt. This gives accountability for configuration changes.

6) TemplateConfig
Fields should include templateName, language, bodyText, emojiSet, enabled, useBusinessHoursVariant, useUrgentVariant, and updatedAt.

Recommended indexes include unique messageId for idempotency, contactId plus lastAutoReplyAt for cooldown checks, and ownerId for configuration lookup. Message logs can be retained for a limited period to reduce storage usage.

Key flows:
Inbound customer message flow:

1) CookMyBots delivers a normalized inbound WhatsApp message event to the bot brain service.
2) The transport adapter validates the event shape and passes it to the message router.
3) The router ignores unsupported system events and detects whether the sender is the owner/admin.
4) If the message is from the owner, it is passed to the command handler instead of the auto-reply engine.
5) If the message is from a customer, the availability engine checks manual away mode, temporary away sessions, and business-hours rules.
6) If the owner is available, the bot records the message and sends no auto-reply.
7) If the owner is unavailable, the decision engine checks whether the contact is blocked, whether the chat is a group, whether a cooldown is active, and whether this message was already processed.
8) If allowed, the template engine creates a friendly emoji response.
9) The bot sends the response through CookMyBots managed transport.
10) The bot stores the reply timestamp and message decision for future cooldown and audit purposes.

Owner turns away mode on:

1) Owner sends a command such as away on Out for lunch 😊.
2) The command handler verifies that the sender is an authorized admin.
3) The bot updates BotConfig or creates an active AwaySession.
4) The bot confirms to the owner with a short message such as Away mode is now on 😊.
5) Future customer messages receive the configured away response subject to cooldown rules.

Owner turns away mode off:

1) Owner sends away off.
2) The bot disables the active away state.
3) The bot confirms that auto-replies are paused.
4) Future customer messages are logged but not auto-replied unless business-hours rules still mark the owner unavailable.

Cooldown behavior:

1) A customer messages while away mode is active.
2) The bot replies once.
3) If the same customer sends more messages within the cooldown window, the bot does not keep replying.
4) After the cooldown expires, a new message can receive a fresh away reply.

Urgent keyword flow:

1) The away message can tell customers to send URGENT for priority attention.
2) If a customer sends the urgent keyword, the bot can respond with a special acknowledgement and mark the contact as urgent in ContactState.
3) The bot should not promise emergency handling unless the owner explicitly configures that wording.

Tech stack:
The service should be a single Node.js application using ESM modules. It should run as one process and contain the bot logic, command handling, availability rules, template rendering, persistence access, and CookMyBots transport integration.

WhatsApp connectivity should be handled only through CookMyBots managed transport. The bot project should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not require WHATSAPPTOKEN, WHATSAPPPHONENUMBERID, or WHATSAPPVERIFYTOKEN. The service should only need the credentials or connection settings required by CookMyBots for the managed transport.

Persistence should use MongoDB when production durability is needed. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable for local testing, demos, or a personal bot where restart persistence is not required. No additional databases, cache servers, brokers, or external queue systems should be introduced.

For any optional media or export storage, use object storage or simple filesystem storage described generically. This bot does not require image or file storage for the core away-reply use case.

Deployment should be a generic Node.js server in the cloud or any always-on environment capable of running a single Node.js service. Configuration should be provided through environment variables or a secure runtime configuration mechanism. The process should support graceful startup, graceful shutdown, and health checks.

Non-functional requirements:
Reliability:

1) Use messageId-based idempotency so the same inbound message does not trigger duplicate replies.
2) Store lastAutoReplyAt per contact to enforce cooldowns.
3) Fail safely by logging errors and avoiding repeated send attempts that could spam users.
4) Keep default behavior conservative: reply only in direct chats unless group replies are explicitly enabled.

Security:

1) Only authorized owner/admin numbers can run commands.
2) Customer messages should never be able to change bot configuration.
3) Logs should store previews rather than full sensitive conversations where possible.
4) Secrets for CookMyBots and MongoDB should be kept outside source control.

Privacy:

1) Retain only the data needed for reply decisions and support.
2) Allow message logs to expire after a configured retention period.
3) Provide a command or admin operation to clear a contact’s stored state if needed.

User experience:

1) Replies should feel human, concise, and friendly.
2) Emojis should be configurable because some businesses prefer a professional tone while personal users may want a casual tone.
3) The bot should not over-reply during a conversation.
4) The away message should set realistic expectations, such as expected response time or business hours.

Operations:

1) Expose a simple health status for process monitoring.
2) Log structured events for inbound messages, decisions, sends, skips, and command changes.
3) Include safe defaults for cooldown, business hours, and group behavior.
4) Support configuration backup through MongoDB records or simple exported configuration.

Bot commands:
• away on — Enables manual away mode immediately. Customer messages will receive the configured emoji-rich auto-reply, subject to cooldown and contact rules. (usage: away on) [availability]
• away off — Disables manual away mode. The bot stops sending manual away replies, though business-hours rules may still apply if enabled. (usage: away off) [availability]
• away for — Turns on away mode for a temporary duration, then automatically returns to the previous availability state. (usage: away for 2h In a meeting 😊) [availability]
• status — Shows whether the bot is enabled, whether away mode is active, the current away message, cooldown settings, and business-hours status. (usage: status) [admin]
• set message — Updates the default auto-reply text. The message can include emojis and should clearly explain when the owner will respond. (usage: set message Hi 👋 I’m offline right now, but I’ll reply as soon as I can 😊) [configuration]
• set cooldown — Sets how long the bot should wait before sending another away reply to the same contact. (usage: set cooldown 60m) [configuration]
• set hours — Configures business hours so the bot can automatically reply outside the owner’s normal availability window. (usage: set hours Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00) [configuration]
• groups on — Allows away replies in group chats. This should be disabled by default to avoid noisy group behavior. (usage: groups on) [configuration]
• groups off — Disables away replies in group chats. Direct customer chats can still receive replies. (usage: groups off) [configuration]
• preview — Shows the owner exactly what customers will receive if they message while the bot is in away mode. (usage: preview) [testing]

# WhatsApp Away Reply Bot

This is a CookMyBots managed WhatsApp brain service.

CookMyBots handles WhatsApp connection, phone pairing, sessions, and message routing. This project does not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks, Baileys sessions, QR login, or phone pairing.

The bot is an AI-first away auto-reply assistant. When CookMyBots routes a WhatsApp message to this service, the bot uses CookMyBots AI Gateway to generate a brief, friendly WhatsApp-native away reply with appropriate emojis.

## Owner knowledge

The raw owner prompt is preserved exactly as:

Create a bot that automatically responds to messages when not online,with emojis

This is the only source of truth for what the bot knows. The bot must not invent business details, products, prices, contacts, locations, delivery details, payment details, support policies, moderation rules, or community behavior.

If someone asks for details that the owner did not provide, the bot should politely say that the owner has not provided that detail yet.

## Public behavior

There are no slash commands, menus, or command maps.

Users simply send normal WhatsApp messages. The bot replies as an away responder when AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED is enabled.

Public behavior:

1) Responds naturally to WhatsApp DMs routed by CookMyBots.
2) Responds briefly in groups or communities when CookMyBots routes those messages.
3) Acknowledges the incoming message.
4) Explains that the owner is currently unavailable or not online.
5) Invites the sender to wait for a direct reply later.
6) Uses friendly emojis without overusing them.
7) Says clearly when the requested detail was not supplied by the owner.

## Endpoint

CookMyBots calls this endpoint:

POST /webhook/cookmybots/whatsapp

The request must include:

X-CookMyBots-Webhook-Secret: your configured CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET

The endpoint returns:

{ "ok": true, "reply": "..." }

## Environment variables

PORT
The HTTP port. Defaults to 3000.

CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET
Used to verify that inbound webhook calls came from CookMyBots. Configure this in the deployed service environment.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_ENDPOINT
CookMyBots AI Gateway base URL. It must be a base URL such as https://api.cookmybots.com/api/ai. The bot appends /chat itself.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY
CookMyBots AI Gateway key. The bot sends it using Authorization: Bearer, but never logs the key.

AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED
Optional. Defaults to true when missing. Set to false, 0, off, no, or disabled to pause auto replies.

OWNER_DISPLAY_NAME
Optional. Defaults to the owner when missing. Used only to help AI phrase natural away replies.

AI_TIMEOUT_MS
Optional. Defaults to 600000 milliseconds.

AI_MAX_RETRIES
Optional. Defaults to 2 retries.

CONCURRENCY
Optional. Defaults to 20 global simultaneous AI jobs. The bot also uses a per-chat lock so one chat cannot stack multiple AI replies at once.

## Local setup

1) Install dependencies:

npm install

2) Copy the sample environment file:

cp .env.sample .env

3) Fill in CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET and COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY.

4) Start development mode:

npm run dev

## Local test

You can test without WhatsApp transport by using /test:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/test \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hi, are you there?"}'

## Deployment

Deploy as one Node.js service on Render or a similar host.

Use:

Build command: npm run build
Start command: npm start

Do not create a worker process or queue process. This project runs as a single Node.js process.

## Logging

The bot logs startup, environment sanity booleans, managed webhook handling, AI gateway start, AI gateway success, AI gateway failure, and occasional memory usage.

Secrets are never logged.

## Database

No database is required for this version. The bot keeps only a small bounded in-memory conversation context per chat to help AI respond naturally during the current process lifetime.

Bot: WhatsApp Away Auto-Reply Bot with Friendly Emojis

Summary:
A production-ready WhatsApp bot that acts as the account owner’s smart away assistant. When the owner is offline, busy, outside business hours, or manually marked as unavailable, the bot replies automatically with a friendly emoji-rich message, sets expectations, and optionally captures the sender’s request for later follow-up.

The bot is the brain service only. It runs as a single Node.js ESM process and connects to WhatsApp through CookMyBots managed transport. CookMyBots handles the WhatsApp connection and delivery layer, while this service handles rules, state, message decisions, templates, cooldowns, and optional persistence.

Product goals:
The main product goal is to prevent missed WhatsApp conversations from feeling ignored. If someone messages while the owner is unavailable, the bot should respond quickly, warmly, and clearly with emojis such as 😊, 👋, ⏰, or 🙏.

1) Provide automatic away replies when the owner is not online or has enabled away mode.
2) Let the owner configure message text, emojis, business hours, cooldowns, and exceptions.
3) Avoid annoying users by replying only once per contact within a configurable time window.
4) Support simple commands over WhatsApp so the owner can turn away mode on or off without opening an admin dashboard.
5) Keep the behavior safe for production by logging decisions, handling duplicate messages, and preventing response loops.
6) Support both simple personal use and small-business use cases, such as replying with opening hours, estimated response time, and urgent contact instructions.

A good default away response could be: Hi 👋 Thanks for your message! I’m currently offline, but I’ll get back to you as soon as possible 😊 If it’s urgent, please send the word URGENT.

High-level architecture:
The service should be designed as a single Node.js ESM application that receives normalized message events from CookMyBots managed transport and sends response instructions back through the same managed transport integration. It should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not depend on WhatsApp Cloud API environment variables.

The architecture can be split into practical modules inside the same process:

1) Transport adapter: Receives inbound message events from CookMyBots and sends outbound messages through CookMyBots. This module should hide transport details from the rest of the bot.

2) Message router: Classifies messages as owner commands, normal customer messages, group messages, media messages, repeated messages, or unsupported events.

3) Availability engine: Decides whether the owner is available. It should combine manual away mode, business-hours rules, temporary snooze periods, and optional inactivity-based status.

4) Auto-reply decision engine: Decides whether to reply. It checks availability, contact allowlists or blocklists, group settings, cooldown windows, previous replies, and anti-loop protection.

5) Template engine: Selects and renders a friendly response using the configured text, emojis, sender name if available, current time context, and optional urgency instructions.

6) Command handler: Allows the owner to control the bot from WhatsApp using commands such as away on, away off, status, set message, and set hours.

7) Persistence layer: Uses MongoDB for production persistence if available. For a minimal setup, simple in-memory maps can be used, but they reset on service restart and are best for testing or lightweight personal use.

8) Observability and audit logs: Records key decisions such as inbound message received, reply skipped due to cooldown, reply sent, owner command applied, and configuration changed.

The bot should treat the owner’s own WhatsApp number as an admin identity. Admin messages are commands and should never trigger an away auto-reply. Customer messages are evaluated against the away rules.

Data model:
The data model should be small and focused. MongoDB is recommended for production so configuration, cooldowns, and reply history survive restarts. In-memory maps can be used for a simpler prototype.

1) BotConfig
Fields should include ownerId, botEnabled, awayModeEnabled, awayMessage, emojiStyle, businessHours, timezone, replyCooldownMinutes, respondInGroups, respondToUnknownOnly, urgentKeyword, updatedAt, and createdAt.

2) ContactState
Fields should include contactId, displayName, lastInboundAt, lastAutoReplyAt, lastMessagePreview, isBlocked, isVip, tags, conversationStatus, and updatedAt. This allows per-contact cooldowns and exceptions.

3) AwaySession
Fields should include ownerId, active, reason, startedAt, endsAt, createdByCommand, and temporaryMessageOverride. This supports temporary away states like away for 2 hours.

4) MessageLog
Fields should include messageId, direction, contactId, messageType, textPreview, receivedAt, decision, replySent, skipReason, and relatedCommand. This is useful for debugging and duplicate handling.

5) CommandAudit
Fields should include commandName, issuedBy, rawText, success, errorMessage, configChanges, and createdAt. This gives accountability for configuration changes.

6) TemplateConfig
Fields should include templateName, language, bodyText, emojiSet, enabled, useBusinessHoursVariant, useUrgentVariant, and updatedAt.

Recommended indexes include unique messageId for idempotency, contactId plus lastAutoReplyAt for cooldown checks, and ownerId for configuration lookup. Message logs can be retained for a limited period to reduce storage usage.

Key flows:
Inbound customer message flow:

1) CookMyBots delivers a normalized inbound WhatsApp message event to the bot brain service.
2) The transport adapter validates the event shape and passes it to the message router.
3) The router ignores unsupported system events and detects whether the sender is the owner/admin.
4) If the message is from the owner, it is passed to the command handler instead of the auto-reply engine.
5) If the message is from a customer, the availability engine checks manual away mode, temporary away sessions, and business-hours rules.
6) If the owner is available, the bot records the message and sends no auto-reply.
7) If the owner is unavailable, the decision engine checks whether the contact is blocked, whether the chat is a group, whether a cooldown is active, and whether this message was already processed.
8) If allowed, the template engine creates a friendly emoji response.
9) The bot sends the response through CookMyBots managed transport.
10) The bot stores the reply timestamp and message decision for future cooldown and audit purposes.

Owner turns away mode on:

1) Owner sends a command such as away on Out for lunch 😊.
2) The command handler verifies that the sender is an authorized admin.
3) The bot updates BotConfig or creates an active AwaySession.
4) The bot confirms to the owner with a short message such as Away mode is now on 😊.
5) Future customer messages receive the configured away response subject to cooldown rules.

Owner turns away mode off:

1) Owner sends away off.
2) The bot disables the active away state.
3) The bot confirms that auto-replies are paused.
4) Future customer messages are logged but not auto-replied unless business-hours rules still mark the owner unavailable.

Cooldown behavior:

1) A customer messages while away mode is active.
2) The bot replies once.
3) If the same customer sends more messages within the cooldown window, the bot does not keep replying.
4) After the cooldown expires, a new message can receive a fresh away reply.

Urgent keyword flow:

1) The away message can tell customers to send URGENT for priority attention.
2) If a customer sends the urgent keyword, the bot can respond with a special acknowledgement and mark the contact as urgent in ContactState.
3) The bot should not promise emergency handling unless the owner explicitly configures that wording.

Tech stack:
The service should be a single Node.js application using ESM modules. It should run as one process and contain the bot logic, command handling, availability rules, template rendering, persistence access, and CookMyBots transport integration.

WhatsApp connectivity should be handled only through CookMyBots managed transport. The bot project should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not require WHATSAPPTOKEN, WHATSAPPPHONENUMBERID, or WHATSAPPVERIFYTOKEN. The service should only need the credentials or connection settings required by CookMyBots for the managed transport.

Persistence should use MongoDB when production durability is needed. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable for local testing, demos, or a personal bot where restart persistence is not required. No additional databases, cache servers, brokers, or external queue systems should be introduced.

For any optional media or export storage, use object storage or simple filesystem storage described generically. This bot does not require image or file storage for the core away-reply use case.

Deployment should be a generic Node.js server in the cloud or any always-on environment capable of running a single Node.js service. Configuration should be provided through environment variables or a secure runtime configuration mechanism. The process should support graceful startup, graceful shutdown, and health checks.

Non-functional requirements:
Reliability:

1) Use messageId-based idempotency so the same inbound message does not trigger duplicate replies.
2) Store lastAutoReplyAt per contact to enforce cooldowns.
3) Fail safely by logging errors and avoiding repeated send attempts that could spam users.
4) Keep default behavior conservative: reply only in direct chats unless group replies are explicitly enabled.

Security:

1) Only authorized owner/admin numbers can run commands.
2) Customer messages should never be able to change bot configuration.
3) Logs should store previews rather than full sensitive conversations where possible.
4) Secrets for CookMyBots and MongoDB should be kept outside source control.

Privacy:

1) Retain only the data needed for reply decisions and support.
2) Allow message logs to expire after a configured retention period.
3) Provide a command or admin operation to clear a contact’s stored state if needed.

User experience:

1) Replies should feel human, concise, and friendly.
2) Emojis should be configurable because some businesses prefer a professional tone while personal users may want a casual tone.
3) The bot should not over-reply during a conversation.
4) The away message should set realistic expectations, such as expected response time or business hours.

Operations:

1) Expose a simple health status for process monitoring.
2) Log structured events for inbound messages, decisions, sends, skips, and command changes.
3) Include safe defaults for cooldown, business hours, and group behavior.
4) Support configuration backup through MongoDB records or simple exported configuration.

Bot commands:
• away on — Enables manual away mode immediately. Customer messages will receive the configured emoji-rich auto-reply, subject to cooldown and contact rules. (usage: away on) [availability]
• away off — Disables manual away mode. The bot stops sending manual away replies, though business-hours rules may still apply if enabled. (usage: away off) [availability]
• away for — Turns on away mode for a temporary duration, then automatically returns to the previous availability state. (usage: away for 2h In a meeting 😊) [availability]
• status — Shows whether the bot is enabled, whether away mode is active, the current away message, cooldown settings, and business-hours status. (usage: status) [admin]
• set message — Updates the default auto-reply text. The message can include emojis and should clearly explain when the owner will respond. (usage: set message Hi 👋 I’m offline right now, but I’ll reply as soon as I can 😊) [configuration]
• set cooldown — Sets how long the bot should wait before sending another away reply to the same contact. (usage: set cooldown 60m) [configuration]
• set hours — Configures business hours so the bot can automatically reply outside the owner’s normal availability window. (usage: set hours Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00) [configuration]
• groups on — Allows away replies in group chats. This should be disabled by default to avoid noisy group behavior. (usage: groups on) [configuration]
• groups off — Disables away replies in group chats. Direct customer chats can still receive replies. (usage: groups off) [configuration]
• preview — Shows the owner exactly what customers will receive if they message while the bot is in away mode. (usage: preview) [testing]

3) Avoid annoying users by replying only once per contact within a configurable time window.
4) Support simple commands over WhatsApp so the owner can turn away mode on or off without opening an admin dashboard.
5) Keep the behavior safe for production by logging decisions, handling duplicate messages, and preventing response loops.
6) Support both simple personal use and small-business use cases, such as replying with opening hours, estimated response time, and urgent contact instructions.

A good default away response could be: Hi 👋 Thanks for your message! I’m currently offline, but I’ll get back to you as soon as possible 😊 If it’s urgent, please send the word URGENT.
planSections.highLevelArchitecture:
The service should be designed as a single Node.js ESM application that receives normalized message events from CookMyBots managed transport and sends response instructions back through the same managed transport integration. It should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not depend on WhatsApp Cloud API environment variables.

The architecture can be split into practical modules inside the same process:

1) Transport adapter: Receives inbound message events from CookMyBots and sends outbound messages through CookMyBots. This module should hide transport details from the rest of the bot.

2) Message router: Classifies messages as owner commands, normal customer messages, group messages, media messages, repeated messages, or unsupported events.

3) Availability engine: Decides whether the owner is available. It should combine manual away mode, business-hours rules, temporary snooze periods, and optional inactivity-based status.

4) Auto-reply decision engine: Decides whether to reply. It checks availability, contact allowlists or blocklists, group settings, cooldown windows, previous replies, and anti-loop protection.

5) Template engine: Selects and renders a friendly response using the configured text, emojis, sender name if available, current time context, and optional urgency instructions.

6) Command handler: Allows the owner to control the bot from WhatsApp using commands such as away on, away off, status, set message, and set hours.

7) Persistence layer: Uses MongoDB for production persistence if available. For a minimal setup, simple in-memory maps can be used, but they reset on service restart and are best for testing or lightweight personal use.

8) Observability and audit logs: Records key decisions such as inbound message received, reply skipped due to cooldown, reply sent, owner command applied, and configuration changed.

The bot should treat the owner’s own WhatsApp number as an admin identity. Admin messages are commands and should never trigger an away auto-reply. Customer messages are evaluated against the away rules.
planSections.dataModel:
The data model should be small and focused. MongoDB is recommended for production so configuration, cooldowns, and reply history survive restarts. In-memory maps can be used for a simpler prototype.

1) BotConfig
Fields should include ownerId, botEnabled, awayModeEnabled, awayMessage, emojiStyle, businessHours, timezone, replyCooldownMinutes, respondInGroups, respondToUnknownOnly, urgentKeyword, updatedAt, and createdAt.

2) ContactState
Fields should include contactId, displayName, lastInboundAt, lastAutoReplyAt, lastMessagePreview, isBlocked, isVip, tags, conversationStatus, and updatedAt. This allows per-contact cooldowns and exceptions.

3) AwaySession
Fields should include ownerId, active, reason, startedAt, endsAt, createdByCommand, and temporaryMessageOverride. This supports temporary away states like away for 2 hours.

4) MessageLog
Fields should include messageId, direction, contactId, messageType, textPreview, receivedAt, decision, replySent, skipReason, and relatedCommand. This is useful for debugging and duplicate handling.

5) CommandAudit
Fields should include commandName, issuedBy, rawText, success, errorMessage, configChanges, and createdAt. This gives accountability for configuration changes.

6) TemplateConfig
Fields should include templateName, language, bodyText, emojiSet, enabled, useBusinessHoursVariant, useUrgentVariant, and updatedAt.

Recommended indexes include unique messageId for idempotency, contactId plus lastAutoReplyAt for cooldown checks, and ownerId for configuration lookup. Message logs can be retained for a limited period to reduce storage usage.
planSections.keyFlows:
Inbound customer message flow:

1) CookMyBots delivers a normalized inbound WhatsApp message event to the bot brain service.
2) The transport adapter validates the event shape and passes it to the message router.
3) The router ignores unsupported system events and detects whether the sender is the owner/admin.
4) If the message is from the owner, it is passed to the command handler instead of the auto-reply engine.
5) If the message is from a customer, the availability engine checks manual away mode, temporary away sessions, and business-hours rules.
6) If the owner is available, the bot records the message and sends no auto-reply.
7) If the owner is unavailable, the decision engine checks whether the contact is blocked, whether the chat is a group, whether a cooldown is active, and whether this message was already processed.
8) If allowed, the template engine creates a friendly emoji response.
9) The bot sends the response through CookMyBots managed transport.
10) The bot stores the reply timestamp and message decision for future cooldown and audit purposes.

Owner turns away mode on:

1) Owner sends a command such as away on Out for lunch 😊.
2) The command handler verifies that the sender is an authorized admin.
3) The bot updates BotConfig or creates an active AwaySession.
4) The bot confirms to the owner with a short message such as Away mode is now on 😊.
5) Future customer messages receive the configured away response subject to cooldown rules.

Owner turns away mode off:

1) Owner sends away off.
2) The bot disables the active away state.
3) The bot confirms that auto-replies are paused.
4) Future customer messages are logged but not auto-replied unless business-hours rules still mark the owner unavailable.

Cooldown behavior:

1) A customer messages while away mode is active.
2) The bot replies once.
3) If the same customer sends more messages within the cooldown window, the bot does not keep replying.
4) After the cooldown expires, a new message can receive a fresh away reply.

Urgent keyword flow:

1) The away message can tell customers to send URGENT for priority attention.
2) If a customer sends the urgent keyword, the bot can respond with a special acknowledgement and mark the contact as urgent in ContactState.
3) The bot should not promise emergency handling unless the owner explicitly configures that wording.

The service should be a single Node.js application using ESM modules. It should run as one process and contain the bot logic, command handling, availability rules, template rendering, persistence access, and CookMyBots transport integration.

WhatsApp connectivity should be handled only through CookMyBots managed transport. # WhatsApp Away Reply Bot

This is a CookMyBots managed WhatsApp brain service.

CookMyBots handles WhatsApp connection, phone pairing, sessions, and message routing. This project does not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks, Baileys sessions, QR login, or phone pairing.

The bot is an AI-first away auto-reply assistant. When CookMyBots routes a WhatsApp message to this service, the bot uses CookMyBots AI Gateway to generate a brief, friendly WhatsApp-native away reply with appropriate emojis.

## Owner knowledge

The raw owner prompt is preserved exactly as:

Create a bot that automatically responds to messages when not online,with emojis

This is the only source of truth for what the bot knows. The bot must not invent business details, products, prices, contacts, locations, delivery details, payment details, support policies, moderation rules, or community behavior.

If someone asks for details that the owner did not provide, the bot should politely say that the owner has not provided that detail yet.

## Public behavior

There are no slash commands, menus, or command maps.

Users simply send normal WhatsApp messages. The bot replies as an away responder when AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED is enabled.

Public behavior:

1) Responds naturally to WhatsApp DMs routed by CookMyBots.
2) Responds briefly in groups or communities when CookMyBots routes those messages.
3) Acknowledges the incoming message.
4) Explains that the owner is currently unavailable or not online.
5) Invites the sender to wait for a direct reply later.
6) Uses friendly emojis without overusing them.
7) Says clearly when the requested detail was not supplied by the owner.

## Endpoint

CookMyBots calls this endpoint:

POST /webhook/cookmybots/whatsapp

The request must include:

X-CookMyBots-Webhook-Secret: your configured CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET

The endpoint returns:

{ "ok": true, "reply": "..." }

## Environment variables

PORT
The HTTP port. Defaults to 3000.

CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET
Used to verify that inbound webhook calls came from CookMyBots. Configure this in the deployed service environment.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_ENDPOINT
CookMyBots AI Gateway base URL. It must be a base URL such as https://api.cookmybots.com/api/ai. The bot appends /chat itself.

COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY
CookMyBots AI Gateway key. The bot sends it using Authorization: Bearer, but never logs the key.

AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED
Optional. Defaults to true when missing. Set to false, 0, off, no, or disabled to pause auto replies.

OWNER_DISPLAY_NAME
Optional. Defaults to the owner when missing. Used only to help AI phrase natural away replies.

AI_TIMEOUT_MS
Optional. Defaults to 600000 milliseconds.

AI_MAX_RETRIES
Optional. Defaults to 2 retries.

CONCURRENCY
Optional. Defaults to 20 global simultaneous AI jobs. The bot also uses a per-chat lock so one chat cannot stack multiple AI replies at once.

## Local setup

1) Install dependencies:

npm install

2) Copy the sample environment file:

cp .env.sample .env

3) Fill in CMB_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET and COOKMYBOTS_AI_KEY.

4) Start development mode:

npm run dev

## Local test

You can test without WhatsApp transport by using /test:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/test \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hi, are you there?"}'

## Deployment

Deploy as one Node.js service on Render or a similar host.

Use:

Build command: npm run build
Start command: npm start

Do not create a worker process or queue process. This project runs as a single Node.js process.

## Logging

The bot logs startup, environment sanity booleans, managed webhook handling, AI gateway start, AI gateway success, AI gateway failure, and occasional memory usage.

Secrets are never logged.

## Database

No database is required for this version. The bot keeps only a small bounded in-memory conversation context per chat to help AI respond naturally during the current process lifetime.

4) If the message is from the owner, it is passed to the command handler instead of the auto-reply engine.
5) If the message is from a customer, the availability engine checks manual away mode, temporary away sessions, and business-hours rules.

7) If the owner is unavailable, the decision engine checks whether the contact is blocked, whether the chat is a group, whether a cooldown is active, and whether this message was already processed.
8) If allowed, the template engine creates a friendly emoji response.
9) The bot sends the response through CookMyBots managed transport.
10) The bot stores the reply timestamp and message decision for future cooldown and audit purposes.

3) The bot updates BotConfig or creates an active AwaySession.
4) The bot confirms to the owner with a short message such as Away mode is now on 😊.

1) Owner sends away off.
2) The bot disables the active away state.
3) The bot confirms that auto-replies are paused.
4) Future customer messages are logged but not auto-replied unless business-hours rules still mark the owner unavailable.

1) A customer messages while away mode is active.
2) The bot replies once.
3) If the same customer sends more messages within the cooldown window, the bot does not keep replying.
4) After the cooldown expires, a new message can receive a fresh away reply.

1) The away message can tell customers to send URGENT for priority attention.
2) If a customer sends the urgent keyword, the bot can respond with a special acknowledgement and mark the contact as urgent in ContactState.

Tech stack:
The service should be a single Node.js application using ESM modules. It should run as one process and contain the bot logic, command handling, availability rules, template rendering, persistence access, and CookMyBots transport integration.

WhatsApp connectivity should be handled only through CookMyBots managed transport. The bot project should not implement WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks and should not require WHATSAPPTOKEN, WHATSAPPPHONENUMBERID, or WHATSAPPVERIFYTOKEN. The service should only need the credentials or connection settings required by CookMyBots for the managed transport.

Persistence should use MongoDB when production durability is needed. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable for local testing, demos, or a personal bot where restart persistence is not required. No additional databases, cache servers, brokers, or external queue systems should be introduced.

For any optional media or export storage, use object storage or simple filesystem storage described generically. This bot does not require image or file storage for the core away-reply use case.

Deployment should be a generic Node.js server in the cloud or any always-on environment capable of running a single Node.js service. Configuration should be provided through environment variables or a secure runtime configuration mechanism. The process should support graceful startup, graceful shutdown, and health checks.

Non-functional requirements:
Reliability:

1) Use messageId-based idempotency so the same inbound message does not trigger duplicate replies.
2) Store lastAutoReplyAt per contact to enforce cooldowns.
3) Fail safely by logging errors and avoiding repeated send attempts that could spam users.
4) Keep default behavior conservative: reply only in direct chats unless group replies are explicitly enabled.

Security:

1) Only authorized owner/admin numbers can run commands.
2) Customer messages should never be able to change bot configuration.
3) Logs should store previews rather than full sensitive conversations where possible.
4) Secrets for CookMyBots and MongoDB should be kept outside source control.

Privacy:

1) Retain only the data needed for reply decisions and support.
2) Allow message logs to expire after a configured retention period.
3) Provide a command or admin operation to clear a contact’s stored state if needed.

User experience:

1) Replies should feel human, concise, and friendly.
2) Emojis should be configurable because some businesses prefer a professional tone while personal users may want a casual tone.
3) The bot should not over-reply during a conversation.
4) The away message should set realistic expectations, such as expected response time or business hours.

Operations:

1) Expose a simple health status for process monitoring.
2) Log structured events for inbound messages, decisions, sends, skips, and command changes.
3) Include safe defaults for cooldown, business hours, and group behavior.
4) Support configuration backup through MongoDB records or simple exported configuration.

Bot commands:
• away on — Enables manual away mode immediately. Customer messages will receive the configured emoji-rich auto-reply, subject to cooldown and contact rules. (usage: away on) [availability]
• away off — Disables manual away mode. The bot stops sending manual away replies, though business-hours rules may still apply if enabled. (usage: away off) [availability]
• away for — Turns on away mode for a temporary duration, then automatically returns to the previous availability state. (usage: away for 2h In a meeting 😊) [availability]
• status — Shows whether the bot is enabled, whether away mode is active, the current away message, cooldown settings, and business-hours status. (usage: status) [admin]
• set message — Updates the default auto-reply text. The message can include emojis and should clearly explain when the owner will respond. (usage: set message Hi 👋 I’m offline right now, but I’ll reply as soon as I can 😊) [configuration]
• set cooldown — Sets how long the bot should wait before sending another away reply to the same contact. (usage: set cooldown 60m) [configuration]
• set hours — Configures business hours so the bot can automatically reply outside the owner’s normal availability window. (usage: set hours Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00) [configuration]
• groups on — Allows away replies in group chats. This should be disabled by default to avoid noisy group behavior. (usage: groups on) [configuration]
• groups off — Disables away replies in group chats. Direct customer chats can still receive replies. (usage: groups off) [configuration]
• preview — Shows the owner exactly what customers will receive if they message while the bot is in away mode. (usage: preview) [testing]
